title: A later statement supersedes an earlier one
about: The example from the Cognee draft §3.5: one transcript supports Tuesday status updates, a later one changes the preference to Friday. The second revision supersedes the first. Current reads return Friday; a historical read can still explain Tuesday.

drafts.cognee: §3.1 a correction produces a new revision linked to its predecessor; §3.5 current vs historical reads
drafts.ibm: memories are immutable; logical mutation is override plus invalidation (time travel instead of data loss)
drafts.contextnest: §6.1 editing bumps version, the previous version stays reconstructible; §5.1 pinned reads
